properties.name: Wheatfield (George Rose farm)
properties.period_note: July 1863: standing wheat on 2 July (ripe or nearly ripe; golden-tan).

sources.cite: Historical Marker Database entry for the NPS Wheatfield marker (m=13342): "golden wheat grew tall here in the summer of 1863"
sources.quote_or_paraphrase: NPS marker: golden wheat grew tall here in the summer of 1863; the ground changed hands six times on 2 July.

sources.cite: Warren, G. K. (survey 1868-69, revised 1873 by P. M. Blake), "Battle field of Gettysburg", scale 1:12,000 (reduced from 1:2,400 original, NARA RG 77 E81). Library of Congress Geography and Map Division, call no. G3824.G3 187- W3 (LC Civil War Maps 353.5), image cw0353500, 8878 x 9845 px JPEG2000
sources.quote_or_paraphrase: Open ground enclosed by fences between the woods around the Wheatfield Road (no tree symbols).

properties.method: Hand outline of the open ground on the Warren sheet; the crop (wheat) comes from the marker text and battle accounts.
properties.notes: Measured 19.9 acres; secondary books give about 20 to 26 acres (UNKNOWN which is right). The boundary follows my reading of the Warren fences, not a surveyed corner.
